reviewer_scope: Independent review of pro_data.py, bench.py, public-manifest.json and frontend F1/F2/O2/O4 changes; did not review own approval implementation.

findings.status: closed after source and browser evidence review
findings.trigger: Select an actual valid cached Pro instance whose public fields or official resource cache fail validation.
findings.issue: The new catch branch replaces every HTTP 400 with generic input/search instructions. /api/bench/cached also returns 400 for valid IDs with corrupt caches, so the specific cache repair and download-authorization instructions are hidden.
findings.suggestion: Only replace explicit invalid-ID errors with search guidance; preserve the backend diagnostic for corrupt caches, missing verifier assets and configuration problems.
findings.resolution: checkCachedProblem now preserves error.message for HTTP failures. Read-only source review confirms the catch branch no longer replaces 400 responses with generic ID input instructions.
findings.closure_verification: Frontend browser evidence shows the actual isolated corrupt-cache HTTP 400 repair message, start disabled while corrupt, and start enabled after restoring the valid cache; the production cache SHA256 was unchanged. The independent reviewer inspected source and evidence without repeating browser actions.

independently_verified: Pinned source Parquet SHA256 matches SOURCE_SHA256.
All 642 public-manifest row hashes equal independent canonical hashing of the pinned source public projection.
An original full single-instance cache remains readable offline without the shared projection cache.
A corrupted base_commit is rejected by the read-only cached endpoint and the original damaged file remains byte-identical.
code_and_existing_test_review: Public projection permits exactly public columns, validates every row and rejects duplicate or missing IDs.
Cross-process lock is OS-owned, and interrupted workers release it; prior cache bytes are replaced only after complete verification.
Three-process download coalescing and cancelled-download recovery are covered by actual localhost tests without mocks.
Single-case repair requiring network occurs only after explicit download authorization; valid old caches do not require new source downloads.

frontend_review: Inline evaluation uses request epoch, viewed run identity and generation checks after both asynchronous reads; close/navigation invalidates the plan.
Library detail close and navigation invalidate in-flight successful responses.
Known-cost floor is separated from unknown total cost in the task header.
Partial-patch TimeExceeded and Pro evaluation timeout labels use the correct semantics.
review_limits: Browser tests were intentionally not duplicated while the frontend agent was running them; lock and cancellation tests were reviewed, not rerun by this reviewer.
